publication.title: iPhone OS Research Atlas
publication.scope: iPhone OS 1.1.4 / 4A102 and 3.1.3 / 7E18; native PinePhone execution, distinct QEMU gates and offline next-target study
publication.provenance: Original editorial synthesis of private project notebooks and experiment reports, with reviewed capture images, selected source excerpts and their provenance. Firmware, storage images, complete run artifacts and the implementation repository are not included.
publication.author: Felipe Sabino

record.title: Watchdog controls and clean reboot have different reach
record.method: Deliberate emulator panic/shutdown stalls, compared with recorded physical normal-operation checks
record.observation: The production watchdog has deliberate panic and stalled-shutdown controls in QEMU. Physical normal runs record IRQ petting and a clean BSD/Mach return to recovery.
record.limits: The physical normal-run evidence is not a controlled physical hang or panic test. These controls do not establish recovery from every hardware stall, safe sudden power loss, thermal supervision or automatic battery protection.

records.access: Private project record; only the selected excerpt is distributed

exhibits.title: Watchdog controls and clean reboot have different reach
rows: Normal IRQ petting; clean BSD/Mach reboot
No automatic battery or temperature supervisor
exhibits.interpretation: A fallback watchdog and an orderly filesystem shutdown address different failures. The capability page qualifies unattended recovery accordingly.

excerpts.locator: lines 97–103, ending with the sentence about Jumpdrive
excerpts.content:
The accepted native input module arms A64 WDOG0 for the verified 16-second
reset interval. Its timer-IRQ hook reloads the watchdog during normal running;
BSD shutdown status stops reloads so a stuck shutdown can return to recovery.
The panic path likewise stops normal petting. This is stall/panic recovery,
not thermal or battery supervision. QEMU controls exercise deliberate panic
and shutdown stalls; physical normal runs record live IRQ petting and clean
BSD/Mach reboot to Jumpdrive.
